_about: Files of the verification tooling (playground, catalogue, benchmarks, verifier unit tests, site, demo programs, runtime glue, Wasm differential runner) and the design documents. The directories themselves are described in verification.json and top-level.json, so this file describes their files and the subdirectories those files do not cover. All of this is Vox-only, so entries have `what` only. American spelling.
_sources: The code at HEAD 5c5e606aaf (outside verification/explorer and verification/site identical to trunk a0b99ddfeb): each file's header comment and body, verification/playground/README.md, verification/catalogue/README.md, the catalogue pages' headers, research/mastery-20260927/INDEX.md Part C for the soundness history. Git history for the design documents' staleness (design-docs/ghost.md was not updated by the ghost-field-locality merge a0b99ddfeb).

what.short: How to build, serve and host the playground, how the checker reaches Z3 in the browser, and the limits of the JavaScript build.
long: The build runs only `make boot-compiler runtime-stdlib`: the checker is built in Dune's boot context, whose compiler is the opam switch's, so the switch's js_of_ocaml 6.3.2 accepts the bytecode.

The limitations section is the one to read before trusting a verdict: 32-bit host integers (literals outside [-2^31, 2^31) are declined), single files only with no `-principal` and no `.mli`, a 34 MB Z3 binary that needs cross-origin isolation, and the JavaScript stack.

what.short: The browser driver: voxCheck does what ocamlc -extension refinement_types -c does up to Lambda, on an in-memory file, and returns status, messages and message locations.
long: Status 0 is accepted, 2 rejected and 3 not checked: a limitation of the JavaScript build (a literal the 32-bit host reads differently, or a JavaScript stack overflow) is reported as a limitation of the browser build, with no verdict. With `lambda` set it also returns the erased program as `-dlambda -dcanonical-ids` prints it.
Each check runs in a fresh `Local_store` and resets warnings and the location printer, so a result does not depend on earlier checks.

notes.title: Integer literals on a 32-bit host
notes.text: `target_int` computes a literal's value on the 64-bit target, following `parse_intnat` in `runtime/ints.c`. `check_literal` below compares it with what the host's `int_of_string` gives; where they differ, the file is not checked. The verifier itself models `int` with `Int64` and is unaffected.

notes.title: Where each location is printed
notes.text: The report printer is wrapped so that every location it prints is inside a semantic tag; the tag's marking functions record the byte offset in the captured stderr. The page uses these offsets to turn every location in a message into a link to its range.

notes.title: The erased program
notes.text: Translation, `Slambda.eval` and `Simplif.simplify_lambda_for_bytecode`, printed with canonical identifiers so that the numbering does not depend on identifiers created by earlier checks.

what.short: The browser implementation of the native Vox_smt_solver interface: SMT-LIB text goes to Z3 WebAssembly through globalThis.voxZ3Eval, synchronously, so the verifier runs unchanged.
what.long: Z3's own `:timeout` option stands in for the native runner's wall-clock deadline. The response protocol is shared with the native runner through `Vox_smt_response`.

notes.text: This comment says the page runs every query in one persistent Z3 context. `web/checker.js` in fact deletes the context and creates a new one whenever a query starts with `(reset)`, because an API context keeps counting resources across resets; so each query gets a fresh context and resource limits mean what they mean natively.

what.short: Builds the playground as static files in _build/playground/site: boot compiler and stdlib interfaces, js_of_ocaml, npm packages, examples and optionally the verified library's interfaces.
what.long: `--library-prefix` ships the verified library's 125 interfaces (19 MB) so that programs can use `Vox_sequence` and the rest; the examples do not need them. `--catalogue-url` and `--home-url` set the page's links when it is part of the public site.

Loads Z3 and the checker into one scope and returns a synchronous check function; shared by the browser worker and the Node differential runner.
what.long: It starts Z3's timer threads before any check (a worker cannot start one while synchronous code runs) and unpacks the shipped interfaces into js_of_ocaml's file system from one bundle.

notes.title: A fresh Z3 context per query
notes.text: Every query starts with `(reset)`. A Z3 process restarts its resource count there, but an API context does not, so the context is replaced at each `(reset)`. This keeps the native resource limits meaningful in the browser.

what.short: The Web Worker that runs Z3 and the checker, so a long check does not block the page; it reports the Z3 version, revision and load time once ready.
The playground page: CodeMirror 5 editor, example picker, verdict, diagnostics marked in the editor, links from message locations to source ranges, and the erased Lambda view.
Compares the built playground (run in Node) with an installed native compiler: same status, same complete output, same erased Lambda for accepted examples, and valid printed locations.
long: Inputs are the examples, the integer boundary cases in `cases/`, and every phrase of the expect tests listed in `sample.txt`, each phrase compiled with the earlier phrases its test accepts. A file the browser declines (status 3) is listed as NOT CHECKED; any other difference is a DISAGREE and fails the run.
`--only-native` and `--compare-with` let the native side run on another machine; `--browser-bundle` writes `browser.html` to repeat the comparison in a real browser.

notes.title: Expect tests split into files
notes.text: Each `[%%expect]` phrase becomes one file consisting of that phrase and the earlier phrases the test expects to be accepted, since the playground checks single files.

notes.title: Checking the reported locations
notes.text: Every location the browser reports must be printed at the offsets it claims and denote a valid range in the source, or in an interface source the site ships; and every location line in the output must be one of the reported locations.

One-line boundary programs for the differential check: int literals near 2^31 and 2^62, hexadecimal and nativeint literals, overflow at max_int and min_int, and shift counts.
what.long: These are the inputs where a 32-bit JavaScript host and a 64-bit target can disagree; the browser build must either give the native verdict or decline to check.

what.short: The order, titles and one-line summaries of the eight playground examples shown in the example picker.
The first playground example: clamp with a dependent upper bound, a caller relying on its result refinement, and division through Int.Refined.
x + 1 > x is rejected at max_int because int is a 63-bit machine integer; the variant with x < max_int is accepted.
Int.Refined.( / ) requires a provably nonzero divisor; a divisor that may be 0 is rejected, with a note pointing at the violated refinement in the standard library.
[@def] equations and an inductive lemma about length and append, called inside ghost_ so that the proof is checked and erased.
[@@decreases] measures for Euclid's algorithm and a binary search; the Collatz iteration with measure n is rejected.
A summary record with a ghost list field; the erased Lambda shows that the [@@ ghost] field and the sum_def calls are gone.
An affine ghost permit: firing it once is accepted, firing it twice is a uniqueness error.
unreachable_ () must be proved: accepted for the [] case of a list refined to be nonempty and in an exhaustive sign test, rejected after List.rev of an arbitrary list.

notes.title: The quoting directives

notes.text: A quote names its range by patterns, so that edits elsewhere in the file do not break it and a quote whose pattern stops matching fails the build. The explorer's `from`/`to` ranges follow the same convention.
